results.note: sni.org/culture/history/ (title 'History - SNI'): 'Today, more than 8,500 Seneca citizens and their families continue this legacy'; citizens 'reside in large portions of Western New York on the Allegany, Cattaraugus, and Oil Spring territories'. Evidence verbatim.
sni.org home: 'true democracy whose constitution was established in 1848'; 16-member Tribal Council with equal representatives from Cattaraugus and Allegany. Evidence verbatim.
Seneca Language page: Deadiwënöhsnye's Gëjóhgwa' Immersion Program goal is to enable students to converse in Onöndowa'ga:' Gawë:nö'; also classes and online learning. Evidence verbatim.
About Us: 'Onondaga is still governed by our traditional government'; fourteen Onondaga Chiefs and their Clan Mothers caretakers of our land. Evidence verbatim.
About Us: 'lies in the middle of the Haudenosaunee territory and is also known as the Central Fire'; 'located south of the City of Syracuse'. Evidence verbatim.

Government page, Fire Keepers section: Fire Keepers bring the question, and if they agree 'the Fire Keepers announce that we are of One Mind of the issue, we have come to consensus.' Evidence verbatim.

'The Tribal Council is comprised of three Chiefs, three Sub-Chiefs and a Tribal Clerk'; 'formalized elections are now scheduled each year and definite terms of office were established'. Evidence verbatim.
Page: Akwesasne 'translates roughly to "Land where the partridge drums"'. Evidence verbatim.
'Our original homeland is the north eastern region of New York State extending into southern Canada and Vermont.' Evidence verbatim.

About Us: 'governed by a Nation Council of clan representatives'; 'Each clan chooses a representative to join the governing body'. Evidence verbatim. Wording stays close to source but is a plain governance statement.

Language page (title 'Preserving the Onyota'a:ká: language'): intense language courses, preschool curriculum at Early Learning Center, electronic books and smart phone apps, Oneida language keyboard. Evidence verbatim.

America's First Allies page: Oneidas fought alongside the colonists against the British, carried corn to feed Gen. George Washington's starving soldiers; page title 'America's First Allies'. Evidence verbatim.
'The Cayuga Nation has five clans, and every member of our Nation belongs to one.' Evidence verbatim.

Supported (page: citizens returned to live on ancestral homeland for the first time in over 200 years; homeland is in the Finger Lakes region), but the original text nearly copied the source sentence word for word. Reworded; no year is given on the page, so as_of stays null.
results.text: After more than 200 years away, Cayuga Nation citizens once again live on their ancestral homeland in New York's Finger Lakes region.
results.evidence: returned to live on our ancestral homeland for the first time

results.note: Supported (page: Treaty of Canandaigua signed November 11, 1794; 'This historic agreement, still in effect today, secured peace between the United States and the Haudenosaunee'), but original text closely copied that sentence. Reworded.
results.text: Signed in 1794, the Treaty of Canandaigua made peace between the Haudenosaunee and the United States, and it remains in force today.
results.evidence: This historic agreement, still in effect today, secured peace

results.note: Home page: Language Program 'whose mission is to revive a Tuscarora speaking community'. Evidence verbatim.

NMAI Haudenosaunee Guide PDF (text extracted locally): 'In 1722, members of the Tuscarora Nation, who were living in what is now North Carolina, traveled north ... were invited to join the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, becoming its sixth nation.' Evidence verbatim.
Home page: Environment Program 'is a subsidiary of the Haudenosaunee Environmental Task Force' and 'established in 1992 by the Grand Council'. Evidence verbatim.
About The Nation: 'is the largest tribal nation in the country'; 'based in Tahlequah, Oklahoma, the capital of the Cherokee Nation'. Evidence verbatim.
About The Nation: 'consists of three branches: legislative, executive and judicial'; '14-county reservation area'. Evidence verbatim.
Language Department: 'It is not an alphabet, but instead contains 85 distinct characters...'; master-apprentice program and Cherokee Immersion School. Evidence verbatim.
NC DOA Tribal Communities: 'makes its home on the 56,000-acre Qualla Boundary, adjacent to the Great Smoky Mountains National Park'. Evidence verbatim. Page undated; as_of 2026 = date read.
NC DOA: 'There are more than 16,000 enrolled members with over 60% living on the Boundary.' Evidence verbatim.

Page: 'Cherokee is a sovereign nation, meaning it has its own laws, elections, government, institutions, and the like.' Original text nearly copied it and 'Cherokee in North Carolina' was ambiguous (could read as the town). Reworded to name the Eastern Band.
results.text: As a sovereign nation, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians makes its own laws, holds its own elections and runs its own government and institutions.
results.evidence: has its own laws, elections, government, institutions

results.note: About Us: 'Today we number more than 14,000 tribal members strong.' Evidence verbatim.

About Us: 'We are also known as the Western Cherokee, or Old Settlers'; 'The Keetoowahs were the first Cherokees to move west, first voluntarily to avoid encroachment from colonizers'. Evidence verbatim.
Home: 'The UKB Tribal Council is comprised of four officers and nine district representatives.' Tahlequah in page title. Evidence verbatim.
Home: '100K CITIZENS AND GROWING'. Evidence verbatim (4 words, uppercase on page).

Mvskoke Language Program page: 'we provide language resources and classes to the Mvskoke people to preserve our language, culture, and sovereignty.' Evidence verbatim.

Page: 'The addition of two new reservations (Tampa and Immokalee) brought Seminole federal trust holdings in Florida to more than 90,000 acres.' The passage is undated (James Billie era), so 'now total' and as_of 2026 are not supported. Reworded to the page's framing; set as_of to null.
results.text: Adding the Tampa and Immokalee reservations brought the Seminole Tribe of Florida's federal trust lands to more than 90,000 acres.
results.evidence: Seminole federal trust holdings in Florida to more than 90,000 acres

results.note: Page: 'the Tribal Council is the chief governing body', 'composed of a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and Council Representatives from each reservation'. The Board is mentioned only once in passing, so 'working alongside the Tribal Board' is not supported. Corrected composition.
results.text: The Tribal Council, with a Chairman, a Vice-Chairman and representatives from each reservation, is the chief governing body of the Seminole Tribe of Florida.
results.evidence: the Tribal Council is the chief governing body

About: 'Covering 10,864 square miles, encompassing eight whole counties and parts of five counties in Southeastern Oklahoma.' Evidence verbatim.

Our Nation: 'You'll find five distinct ecoregions within our 13 counties'. Evidence verbatim.

Supported (pottery 'formed completely by hand'; 'Even though societal changes led to a decline of pottery making, the tradition has been revived and is still passed down today'), but original text copied the source clause nearly verbatim. Reworded.
results.text: Catawba potters shape every piece by hand. The craft declined for a while, but it was revived and new generations keep learning it.
results.evidence: the tradition has been revived and is still passed down today

results.note: About: 'There are currently over 3300 enrolled members of the Nation.' The 'continues to grow' part comes from a separate sentence on the same page ('over 3000 enrolled tribal citizens and continue to grow'). Both on page; evidence verbatim.

Supported (home: 'We are the People of the Dark Water'; 'The Lumbee People are known for their entrepreneurial spirit and their focus on education'), but original text was a near-verbatim copy. Reworded.

names.note: sni.org uses 'The Seneca Nation' (heading) and 'Seneca Nation of Indians' (title). Pronounce 'SEN-i-ka' is verbatim in the NMAI Haudenosaunee Guide, but that is not the Nation's own source; the project plan says pronunciation appears only where the nation's own sources give one, so consider setting pronounce to null.

About Us asks to be called 'Onondaga, Onondaga Nation, Onondaga people, Haudenosaunee'; asks to avoid 'Indian' and 'tribe/tribal' (facts comply). Pronounce 'on-nen-DA-ga' and 'Onundagaono'/'People of the Hills'/'Keepers of the Central Fire' verified in NMAI guide; pronounce is not from the Nation's own source (see policy note on Seneca).

srmt-nsn.gov: 'The Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe is the federally-recognized government of the Saint Regis Mohawk Reservation at Akwesasne.' Pronounce 'MO-hawk' and Kanien'kehaka/People of the Flint/Keepers of the Eastern Door verified in NMAI guide; pronounce not from the Tribe's own source.
Site self-name 'Oneida Indian Nation'. Pronounce 'o-NY-da', Onayotekaono, People of the Standing Stone verified in NMAI guide; pronounce not from the Nation's own source.
Site uses 'Cayuga Nation' ('Welcome To Cayuga Nation'). Pronounce 'ka-YOO-ga', Guyohkohnyoh, People of the Great Swamp verified in NMAI guide; pronounce not from the Nation's own source.
Site uses 'Tuscarora Nation'. Pronounce 'tus-ka-ROR-a', Skaruhreh, The Shirt Wearing People verified in NMAI guide; pronounce not from the Nation's own source.

ebci.gov title 'Home - Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians'; also uses EBCI.

Home title 'Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe | People of the First Light'.
